stem.en: Kabir wires the zinc strip and the copper strip together with a bare wire, no LED, and the LED is not lit because there is no LED. He says "no electricity is flowing". What is happening?

text.en: Electrons are flowing hard through the bare wire, and the zinc is dissolving fast. Without a load the energy of the fall turns into a little heat in the wire and the water.

feedback.en: A bulb shows current; it does not cause it. The bare wire carries more current than the LED did, since nothing slows it.
The zinc dissolves faster. The reaction runs as long as electrons have any path at all.
The direction is set by the ladder. Zinc gives, copper receives, wire or no wire.

explanation.en: Current needs a path and a push. The bare wire is a path; the difference between the metals is the push. The LED was only a way to make the flow do something useful.
